facts.finding: The campaign is structured as: Prologue: The Vestibule, then 16 numbered chapters (Chapter I through Chapter XVI), then Epilogue: Requiem — 18 total story chapters. A 19th, secret bonus chapter (Lost Chapter: Angel Slayer) exists outside the main story. Chapters are subdivided into individual fight/exploration segments called 'Verses'.
facts.source: Aggregated from bayonetta.fandom.com/wiki/Walkthrough chapter sub-pages (individually confirmed titles for Chapters IV, VII, XI, XIII, XIV, XV, XVI, Prologue, Epilogue), cross-checked against gamerant.com 'Bayonetta 1: How Many Chapters Does It Have' and neoseeker/trueachievements walkthrough listings.
facts.notes: Direct page fetches to fandom/neoseeker/trueachievements returned HTTP 402/403 in this session; this list is reconstructed from WebSearch result snippets referencing those pages, not a single primary-source read. Recommend a direct verification pass if possible.

facts.finding: Prologue: The Vestibule / Chapter I: The Angel's Metropolis / Chapter II: Vigrid, City of Déjà vu / Chapter III: The Burning Ground / Chapter IV: The Cardinal Virtue of Fortitude / Chapter V: The Lost Holy Grounds / Chapter VI: The Gates of Paradise / Chapter VII: The Cardinal Virtue of Temperance / Chapter VIII: Route 666 / Chapter IX: Paradiso - A Remembrance of Time / Chapter X: Paradiso - A Sea of Stars / Chapter XI: The Cardinal Virtue of Justice / Chapter XII: The Broken Sky / Chapter XIII: The Cardinal Virtue of Prudence / Chapter XIV: Isla Del Sol / Chapter XV: A Tower to Truth / Chapter XVI: The Lumen Sage / Epilogue: Requiem / (secret) Lost Chapter: Angel Slayer.
facts.source: WebSearch synthesis of bayonetta.fandom.com walkthrough page titles and strategywiki.org/wiki/Bayonetta/Table_of_Contents listing (fetch of strategywiki itself failed with 403; relied on search snippet).

facts.finding: Could not confirm exact number of verses per individual story chapter, nor the total verse count across the full campaign.

Fortitudo, 'Bringer of Flame' — Cardinal Virtue of Fortitude, one of the four Auditio (highest-ranking angels) of the Hierarchy of Laguna. Fought in Chapter IV: The Cardinal Virtue of Fortitude. Mandatory main-path boss.
facts.trackable: Not independently confirmed beyond general Verse medal tracking (see ranking system).

facts.finding: Temperantia, 'Manipulator of Wind' — Cardinal Virtue of Temperance, one of the four Auditio. Fought in Chapter VII: The Cardinal Virtue of Temperance, in a tornado arena. Mandatory main-path boss.

Iustitia (spelled 'Iustitia' on the wiki, sometimes rendered 'Justitia') — Cardinal Virtue of Justice, one of the four Auditio. Fought in Chapter XI: The Cardinal Virtue of Justice. Mandatory main-path boss.

Sapientia — Cardinal Virtue of Prudence, one of the four Auditio. Fought in Chapter XIII: The Cardinal Virtue of Prudence; fight involves surfing across water and damaging Sapientia's legs before an infernal-demon-summon finisher. Mandatory main-path boss.
sources: goombastomp.com boss ranking article (via search snippet)

facts.finding: Father Balder — Bayonetta's biological father and the last Lumen Sage; orchestrates the plot to resurrect Jubileus. During the resurrection ritual he seals the 'God of Chaos' (Loptr) inside himself, becoming 'Father Balder', whom Bayonetta must defeat. Fought in Chapter XVI: The Lumen Sage. Mandatory main-path boss, penultimate major fight.
sources: namu.wiki Loki(Bayonetta) page and bayonetta.fandom.com/wiki/Loki (via search snippet synthesis)
facts.notes: The exact in-game boss-name display (whether the game itself labels this fight 'Father Balder' vs simply 'Balder') was not directly confirmed from a primary source; the Loptr-sealing/'Father Balder' framing comes from secondary wiki synthesis, not a verified direct quote.

facts.finding: Jubileus the Creator — the true final boss, ruler of Paradiso, resurrected by Father Balder. Fought in Epilogue: Requiem. Bayonetta defeats Jubileus by summoning the demon Queen Sheba to punch the deity's soul into the sun, then destroys its descending physical body with Jeanne's help. Mandatory, final story boss.

Jeanne — rival Umbra Witch, fought as a boss multiple times across the campaign (not a single encounter). Later revealed to have been mind-controlled by Balder/Cardinal Virtues and becomes an ally. Mandatory, recurring.

Joy — a Seraphim-class angel (capable of shapeshifting/splitting into multiple forms) that Bayonetta fights early in the game in what is described as a 'vogue show-off battle' with no real second phase. Exact chapter placement not confirmed.

Fairness, Beloved, and 'Grace and Glory' are recurring angel enemy types that function as repeated mid-tier boss/mini-boss encounters across multiple chapters of Bayonetta 1 (not one-time unique deity fights like the Cardinal Virtues).
sources: WebSearch synthesis of bayonetta.fandom.com enemy pages
facts.notes: Could not verify exact chapters/verses where each appears, nor whether all three are exclusive to Bayonetta 1 vs also/only in Bayonetta 2. 'Golem' and 'Glamor' appear in search results tagged as Bayonetta 2-specific content — do NOT assume they are Bayonetta 1 bosses without further verification.

facts.finding: Lost Chapter: Angel Slayer — a plot-less, secret bonus chapter/survival gauntlet unlocked after finding and completing all 21 Alfheim Portal challenges scattered through the main campaign. Consists of 51 enemy-wave fights split across 5 verses, playable at Normal, Hard, and Non-Stop Infinite Climax difficulty tiers. First-time completion unlocks the demon 'King Zero' as a playable/summonable character. Fully optional, does not block main-story completion.
sources: chaptercheats.com and supercheats.com unlock pages (via search snippet)

facts.finding: 21 Alfheim Portals are hidden throughout the main campaign's chapters. Each is a short, timed combat/platforming challenge (e.g., defeat all enemies before time runs out, no Witch Time allowed, limited move-set restrictions). Completing all 21 unlocks the Lost Chapter.
facts.trackable: Not confirmed whether a dedicated in-game counter/checklist of found vs. total Alfheim portals exists on a menu screen.
facts.missable: unknown — not confirmed whether portals are permanently missable if a chapter is completed without finding them, or remain accessible via chapter replay.

facts.finding: Five difficulty modes, in ascending order: Very Easy, Easy, Normal, Hard, and the hardest mode referred to on the Bayonetta Wiki as '∞ Climax' (rendered in various secondary sources as 'Non-Stop Infinite Climax' or 'Non-Stop ∞ Climax'). Normal is available from the start. Hard unlocks after completing ALL chapters on Normal. The hardest mode unlocks after completing ALL chapters on Hard.
facts.notes: The exact in-game menu text for the hardest difficulty could not be confirmed with certainty — sources disagree between '∞ Climax', 'Infinite Climax', and 'Non-Stop Infinite Climax'. Recommend confirming the literal on-screen string before naming a trophy after it.

facts.finding: The alternate naming convention '1st Climax / 2nd Climax / 3rd Climax' (mapping to Easy/Normal/Hard respectively) that was referenced in the task brief appears, per search results, to be terminology specifically documented for BAYONETTA 2, not clearly confirmed as the in-game naming for the original Bayonetta (2009)/Wii U port. Multiple sources describe Bayonetta 1's difficulty screen simply as Very Easy / Easy / Normal / Hard / ∞ Climax without the '1st/2nd/3rd Climax' labels.
facts.notes: This is a direct contradiction flag against the task brief's assumption — do not build trophy names around 'Third Climax' etc. for Bayonetta 1 without further primary-source confirmation (e.g. an actual screenshot of the Wii U difficulty select menu).

facts.finding: Very Easy: health regenerates over time, plus the 'Immortal Marionette' accessory is auto-equipped (prevents permanent death). Easy: also auto-equips Immortal Marionette. Hardest mode (∞ Climax): enemy placement similar to Hard but with more enemy health, and Witch Time is disabled.

Each Verse is graded with a medal upon completion: Stone, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Pure Platinum (highest). Grading considers time taken, combo/combat score, and damage taken. Pure Platinum specifically requires taking zero damage during the verse in addition to a fast clear time and high combo score. Chapter-level performance is generally described as an average/rounding of that chapter's verse medals; using consumable items (lollipops, Red Hot Shots) or dying counts against the rank.
facts.trackable: Tracked per-verse and viewable after the fact via an in-game 'Play History' / chapter-select detail view that shows medals earned per verse within a chapter.
sources: gamefaqs.gamespot.com boards 'Chapter Grading Guide and Platinum Rank Tips' and 'Requirements for different medals?' (via search snippet)
gamefaqs.gamespot.com PS3 Q&A 'How do I view the medals of each verse afterwards?'
facts.notes: Exact numeric thresholds (time limits, combo score cutoffs, precise rounding formula for chapter-level award) were not confirmed to precision — only the general medal names, general criteria (time/combo/damage), and that Pure Platinum requires zero damage taken.

facts.finding: Bayonetta 1 does not have a traditional story-resetting 'New Game+' with a special second-playthrough mode. Instead, the game uses a persistent Chapter Select system: once a difficulty is unlocked, the player can replay any chapter (including starting from the Prologue) at any unlocked difficulty while keeping all previously unlocked weapons, accessories, moves, and halos/money earned. Starting a genuinely new save file resets all progress.
sources: gamefaqs.gamespot.com PS3 Q&A 'Once you beat all chapters in easy mode...' and 'Can you change difficulty in chapter select?' forum threads, xboxachievements.com forum (via search snippet)
facts.notes: This is community-forum-sourced consensus, not an official manual/patch-note citation. Recommend treating as reasonably reliable but not airtight.

facts.finding: Bayonetta 1 appears to have a single, non-branching ending. After defeating Jubileus in the Epilogue: Requiem, the story resolves with Bayonetta regaining her full memories, reconciling with Jeanne and Luka, and sending the child Cereza back to her own time. A funeral/epilogue scene (attended by Luka) implies Bayonetta is believed dead before a twist reveals she survived. No alternate ending branches were identified.
facts.notes: Could not find a source dedicated specifically to confirming there is exactly one ending with no hidden/alternate variant tied to completion conditions (e.g., difficulty, collectibles). Treat as likely single-ending but not exhaustively ruled out.

facts.finding: The Wii U release of the original Bayonetta was bundled as a bonus disc with every physical copy of Bayonetta 2 (titled 'Bayonetta 2: Special Edition' as a bundle), released Sept 2014 (Japan) / Oct 2014 (NA/EU); it was later also made available standalone on the Wii U eShop. The Wii U port adds four exclusive Nintendo-themed costumes not present in PS3/360/Steam versions: Peach, Daisy, Samus ('Samus' suit with functional arm cannon and Morph Ball), and Link ('Hero of Hyrule', with a shield-block special move). These were curated by original director Hideki Kamiya and include gameplay-affecting special abilities, not just cosmetic swaps.
sources: nintendolife.com 'We Put Bayonetta 2's Nintendo Outfits to the Test'
vooks.net 'Platinum Games details original Bayonetta Wii U improvements'
facts.notes: This is not core to the campaign/chapter/boss structure beat, but is flagged since it is a genuine Wii U-exclusive content difference relevant to overall trophy planning (likely belongs to a 'systems/collectibles' beat for a wardrobe-type trophy).
